impact: Sampson was seen warming up with the team prior to Saturday's contest, but he was not able to make the field against the 49ers. The 6-foot-4 receiver has not played since Louisiana-Lafayette's season opener against Lamar due to a knee injury. His next chance to return will come against Arkansas State on Saturday.

headline: Records sixth reception
story: Jensen (undisclosed) logged a three-yard reception during Saturday's win at UNC Charlotte.
impact: Even though a one-reception game is not excellent for anybody, the fact that Jansen is back after sitting out multiple matchups bodes well for his October output. He played only one other time in September but flourished, catching all but one of six targets for 77 yards against non-FBS team Lamar. The question is whether Jensen can regularly replicate a similar output against the Sun Belt Conference's other programs. Last year, Jensen logged 29 catches for 231 yards and one touchdown, impressive stats that will be difficult to surpass, though far from impossible.

headline: Three receptions and one carry
story: Chaney (shoulder) logged three receptions for 44 yards and a four-yard carry during Saturday's 34-7 victory versus Charlotte.
impact: In two games for Louisiana-Lafayette this season, Chaney has separately logged three receptions and a carry twice. For the 2026 campaign, he is up to 83 all-purpose yards, 78 receiving and five rushing. Chaney has already surpassed his 2025 output, so his next matter at hand is establishing a regular role for ULL now that his health should no longer be an ongoing problem.

headline: Active in warmups
story: Chaney (shoulder) is present and going through warmups ahead of Saturday's game against UNC Charlotte, per Kevin Foote of The Baton Rouge Advocate.
impact: Chaney has missed two consecutive games but is in line to suit up Saturday given his presence during warmups. The wideout last played in the season opener, where he hauled in three receptions for 34 yards.

headline: Warming up Saturday
story: Jensen (undisclosed) is warming up ahead of Saturday's matchup versus Charlotte, per Kevin Foote of The Baton Rouge Advocate.
impact: Jensen has missed the last three games but should have a chance to make his season debut Saturday. The 6-foot-6 tight end will likely enter the team's starting lineup, if he manages to suit up.

headline: Present in warmups
story: Sampson (knee) is participating in warmups ahead of Saturday's matchup at UNC Charlotte, per Kevin Foote of The Baton Rouge Advocate.
impact: Sampson is looking to return for the first time since Louisiana-Lafayette's season opener, and his availability in warmups is a good sign that he could suit up Saturday. The wideout is positioned to have a role in the passing attack if cleared to play.

headline: Logs another touchdown
story: Blanco logged 11 rushing attempts for 55 yards and one touchdown during Louisiana-Lafayette's win Sunday against UAB.
impact: For each of Blanco's 2026 games until Week 3, he logged a touchdown. Overall, the running back's ongoing season features three TDs from 21 rushing attempts for 78 yards.

headline: Accuracy increases, multiple TDs again
story: Winfield was 15-for-20 passing for 110 yards during Saturday's 21-14 victory against UAB. He also had 19 rushes for 91 yards with two touchdowns.
impact: Winfield's pass accuracy has increased with each of Louisiana-Lafayette's 2026 games, starting with 71.4 percent in Week 1 and going up to 75.0 percent in Week 3. Though the quarterback also logged a season-low 110 passing yards, most of his scoring has come with his feet anyway, and that was the case again Saturday. In back-to-back games, Winfield has recorded 91 rushing yards and two touchdowns.

headline: Not listed on Week 3 depth chart
story: Sampson (knee) isn't listed on Louisiana-Lafayette's depth chart and is not expected to play against UAB on Saturday, Kevin Foote of The Baton Rouge Advocate reports.
impact: Sampson is once again absent from the Ragin' Cajuns' depth chart, indicating that he is set to miss his second straight game. The wideout is expected to have a prominent role in the passing attack this season, but his continued absences are delaying his progress. He will aim to recover in time to return against UNC Charlotte next Saturday.

headline: Available for Week 3
story: Strother (collarbone) is available for Saturday's game against UAB, per Kevin Foote of The Baton Rouge Advocate.
impact: Strother has recovered from the broken collarbone that sidelined him to begin the season. The wideout should step into an immediate role in the passing game, especially with Trenton Chaney (shoulder) and Shelton Sampson (knee) absent from the team's Week 3 depth chart.

headline: Set for another absence
story: Jensen (undisclosed) is not on the depth chart and is not expected to play in Week 3 against UAB, Kevin Foote of The Baton Rouge Advocate reports.
impact: Jensen had 77 receiving yards in Week 1, but he didn't play in Week 2 and is now set for a second straight absence. With the TE sidelined against UAB, Teddy Gawlik and Quandre Coates are in line for more targets in the passing game.

headline: Not on depth chart for Week 3
story: Chaney (shoulder) isn't listed on the depth chart and is not expected to play against UAB on Saturday, Kevin Foote of The Baton Rouge Advocate reports.
impact: Chaney recorded three catches against Lamar in Week 1, but he's now set to miss a second straight game with a shoulder injury. His next chance to play should come at UNC Charlotte in Week 4.

headline: Will be fully back in Week 3
story: Smith was limited last week against USC but will be fully available against UAB in Week 3, according to Shannon Mia Belt of Lafayette Daily Advertiser.
impact: Smith's production took a spike in Week 2, and it's now clear that he played limited snaps against USC. The running back previously logged 10 carries for 84 yards and two touchdowns against Lamar in the opener, showcasing his reliability as a rusher when healthy. He is set to return against UAB with no restrictions, aiming to carve out a role in the Ragin' Cajuns backfield.

headline: Three scores in loss
story: Winfield was 16-for-22 passing for 212 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 49-30 loss versus USC. He also had 14 rushes for 91 yards with two touchdowns.
impact: Winfield connected with Russell Babineaux in the fourth quarter for his lone touchdown pass of the contest. The rushing touchdowns came on one and 32-yard runs. Through two games, Winfield has tossed for 401 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Up next is a home matchup with UAB Blazers.

headline: Scores TD in loss
story: Babineaux reeled in all six targets for 91 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 49-30 loss versus USC.
impact: Babineaux caught his first touchdown pass of the season when he connected with quarterback Lunch Winfield for a 14-yard score in the fourth quarter. Through two games, the wideout has recorded seven receptions and 95 yards.

headline: Out vs. USC
story: Jensen (undisclosed) is out for Saturday's game against USC, according to Kevin Foote of The Baton Rouge Advocate.
impact: Jensen is absent from Louisiana-Lafayette's depth chart for Week 2, ruling the tight end out against USC. In Week 1 against Lamar, he broke out as the team leader in the passing attack, hauling in 77 yards. This is a significant blow to the Ragin' Cajuns, leaving Teddy Gawlik and Quandre Coates in line for an increase in targets due to his absence.

headline: Loses field-goal kicking opportunities
story: Kent has lost field-goal kicking opportunities to Hunter Rioux, Matt Belinson of the Ruston Daily Leader reports.
impact: Kent has missed each of his last two field goal kicks, which he attempted back in Week 2 at LSU and Week 3 against Baylor. The freshman may still be relied on for extra points, as he is 13-for-13 in that category.

headline: Four receptions, one touchdown
story: Mickens logged four receptions (on eight targets) for 63 yards during Louisiana Tech's 36-19 loss Saturday at Baylor. He also recorded two rushing attempts for 14 yards and one tou...
impact: For 2026, Mickens' stats include not only three games but also 13 receptions, more than four averaged per matchup. Even though the wide receiver did not recently log a receiving touchdown, he still scored. Because of Mickens' versatility, his stats also feature three TDs.

headline: Strong showing in Week 3
story: Finley tallied eight receptions (on 13 targets) for 65 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 36-19 defeat against Baylor.
impact: Finley had his best game of the season in the loss to Baylor, posting season-high marks in targets, catches and receiving yards while also scoring his second touchdown of the campaign. The senior TE has looked good in the early stages of the season, catching 14 of his 22 targets for 132 yards and two scores in three appearances. He has a firm grip on the TE1 role as long as he stays healthy.

headline: Shows dual-threat ability
story: Kukuk completed 25 of 44 passes for 223 yards, one touchdown and one interception during Saturday's 36-19 loss versus Baylor. He also had 11 rushes for 75 yards.
impact: Kukuk wasn't particularly sharp in this game, as he completed roughly over 50 percent of his throws, but he still tossed two scores against a superior defense while averaging 6.8 yards per carry on the ground. Kukuk has completed 62.7 percent of his passes in his three appearances in 2026, throwing for 283 yards while posting a 3:1 TD:INT.

headline: Questionable for Oct. 3 vs. Army
story: Baker (hand) is questionable for Louisiana Tech's clash with Army in Week 5 after their bye, per Matt Belinson of the Ruston Daily Leader.
impact: Baker missed the Bulldogs' Week 3 loss to Baylor, and head coach Sonny Crumbie said that the starting gunslinger is "questionable at this point." If he can't go against the Black Knights, Louisiana Tech figures to go with Trey Kukuk once again, who tossed for 233 yards one touchdown and one interceptions with 75 yards on the ground to boot in the loss to Baylor.

headline: Starting Saturday
story: Kukuk will make the start against Baylor on Saturday, per Pete Thamel of ESPN.com.
impact: Kukuk will get the start due to Blake Baker being ruled out due to a hand injury. Kukuk has appeared in both games for the Bulldogs this season, completing all seven of his pass attempts for 60 yards and two touchdowns while adding 52 rushing yards as well.

headline: Out vs Baylor
story: Baker (hand) is out for Saturday's matchup against Baylor, per Pete Thamel of ESPN.com.
impact: Baker's status had been up in the air since he was announced to have suffered a fractured hand following last week's loss to LSU, but he is now confirmed to be out. The 6-foot-5 quarterback has thrown for 360 yards and four touchdowns with one interception through two games for Louisiana Tech. He will be replaced by Trey Kukuk as the starter against the Bears.

headline: Enters after injury
story: Kukuk was 3-for-3 passing for 15 yards during Saturday's 45-14 loss versus LSU.
impact: Kukuk entered following an injury to Blake Baker. He completed all three of his passes in the loss.

headline: Catches TD in loss
story: Mickens gathered in six of nine targets for 101 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 45-14 loss to LSU.
impact: Mickens connected with Blake Baker for a 67-yard score in the fourth quarter. Through two games, Mickens has recorded nine receptions for 234 yards and two touchdowns.

headline: Fractures hand, status in doubt
story: Baker fractured his hand and his status for Week 3 at Baylor is in question, per Matt Belinson of the Ruston Daily Leader.
impact: It's unclear how Baker fractured his hand, but the quarterback reportedly hasn't been ruled out yet for the Bulldogs' big opportunity in Waco this weekend. Baker is off to a good start this season with 360 passing yards and four touchdowns through two games, but if he can't go, expect Trey Kukuk to get the nod under center.

headline: Solid day through the air
story: Richardson compiled five receptions (on six targets) for 85 yards during Saturday's 30-27 loss against Wake Forest.
impact: Richardson has had four solid outings this season but has yet to produce a huge day. With starting quarterback Lincoln Keinholz (undisclosed) set to be a game-time call for Week 5 at NC State, this passing game could take a step back next week.

headline: Solid outing despite loss
story: Hurry compiled eight receptions (on 10 targets) for 71 yards during Saturday's 30-27 loss versus Wake Forest.
impact: Hurry saw the most targets he has all season, and the wideout parlayed that into a solid output despite the loss to Wake Forest. Hurry hasn't been extraordinarily explosive or dynamic this season, but he remains a solid part of this Louisville passing game and will look to stay involved next week on the road at NC State.

headline: Scores in loss
story: Skinner hauled in all four targets for 82 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 30-27 loss to Wake Forest.
impact: Skinner now has a touchdown in three straight games. He only has 13 targets across those games, but he's certainly made the most of them. The tight end will look to make it four in a row next week on the road at NC State.

headline: Limited output in upset loss
story: Brown totaled 12 rushes for 48 yards during Saturday's 30-27 defeat to Wake Forest.
impact: Brown was held in check as Louisville fell at the hands of the Demon Deacons. His backfield mate Isaac Brown was also bottled up, and while it was a forgettable day for the two backs, Keyjuan appears to have seized the RB1 role for the Cardinals. He'll look to bounce back next week on the road at NC State.

headline: Will be game-time decision
story: Louisville's head coach Jeff Brohm announced that Kienholz (undisclosed) will be a game-time decision Saturday at North Carolina State, Matt McGavic of Sports Illustrated reports.
impact: Brohm announced that Kienholz has some kind of problem affecting him but did not exactly disclose the issue. The development comes after he logged a 1-1 TD-INT ratio in Week 4 against Wake Forest, but he still impressed with 27 completions for 324 yards and two rushing TDs. That may have been Kienholz's worst game of September, indicating just how good a quarterback the Cardinals would be missing if he cannot go against North Carolina State.

headline: Sitting out Saturday
story: Egan won't be available for Saturday's clash with Wake Forest, per the ACC availability report.
impact: Egan doesn't have any stats on his ledger since 2024, so his absence shouldn't impact the Cards' offense much Saturday. He has numerous chances to rejoin the action down the road.

headline: Good to go for Week 4
story: Brown (undisclosed) is available for Saturday's game against Wake Forest.
impact: After a few more days to prepare for Week 4, Brown has shed his probable status and will look to continue his recent excellence. Back in Week 3, when Louisville returned to conference play, he dominated against SMU, posting 10 rushing attempts for 163 yards and two touchdowns.

headline: Available for Week 4
story: Richardson (undisclosed) is available for Saturday's game against Wake Forest.
impact: Considering that Richardson was probable for Louisville's upcoming game, him becoming available should come as no surprise. Week 4 will mark his second game of ACC action. In the first matchup, he logged four receptions (on six targets) for 62 yards and a 14-yard carry against SMU. Perhaps playing what has been perceived as an easier Wake Forest will help him significantly boost his statistical production.

headline: Expected to go Saturday
story: Brown (undisclosed) is listed as probable ahead of Saturday's game against Wake Forest.
impact: After a breakout performance against SMU despite being limited to 10 carries, Brown is expected to play against the Demon Deacons on Saturday. The running back has recorded 18 carries for 231 yards and two touchdowns through three games.

headline: Carrying probable tag
story: Richardson (undisclosed) is probable for Saturday's game against Wake Forest.
impact: Richardson has yet to miss a game this season and has been a reliable option in the Cardinals' passing attack, catching 15 passes on 19 targets for 243 yards and a touchdown. The probable tag suggests the senior wideout should be available and handle his regular workload on offense. He's seen at least six targets in every game in 2026.

headline: Scores another TD in win
story: Skinner gathered in 3 of 4 targets for 29 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 41-31 win against Southern Methodist.
impact: Skinner doesn't have more than three catches in a single game this fall, but he's scored in back-to-back outings as Louisville has bounced back nicely from the season-opening loss to Ole Miss. The tight end will look to remain a go-to target in the red zone in Week 4 against Wake Forest.

headline: Solid outing in win vs. SMU
story: Richardson accrued four receptions (on six targets) for 62 yards during Saturday's 41-31 victory against Southern Methodist.
impact: Richardson failed to score for the second straight week, but he remained a steady factor in the Cardinals' passing game. Against SMU, however, it was all about Louisville's running game, which gashed the Mustangs all afternoon. Richardson will look to continue his strong start to the season -- and get back in the end zone -- against Wake Forest in Week 4.

headline: Finds end zone in big win
story: McCoy reeled in 4 of 7 targets for 62 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 41-31 victory over Southern Methodist.
impact: McCoy has now scored in each of Louisville's firs three games. The wideout has been a pretty consistent part of this passing game, and through his first three games, he's logged, 62 yards, 102 yards and 62 yards, respectively. Especially with how good the Cardinals' new quarterback Lincoln Kienholz looks, McCoy is certainly worth keeping an eye on fantasy-wise.

headline: Huge day in win over TAMU
story: Harris tallied six receptions (on seven targets) for 163 yards and two touchdowns during Saturday's 35-6 victory against Texas A&M.
impact: Harris had his best game since joining the Tigers as he racked up his first 100 yard game and added his first two touchdowns on the season. Harris hasn't been overly impactful to this point as he has just one other game with multiple catches. With two games now of 80+ yards it is encouraging for the junior wide out.

headline: Touchdown in win over TAMU
story: Jones tallied 14 rushes for 63 yards and one touchdown and caught 3 of 5 targets for 22 yards during Saturday's 35-6 victory against Texas A&M.
impact: Jones had a solid game on 14 carries but saw a bit more of his workload go to Harlem Berry in this one. Most of Berry's work came down the stretch after the game had more or less gotten out of reach, so there is likely no concern that this will become a trend moving forward.

headline: Two touchdowns in relief against TAMU
story: Clark completed 0 of 5 passes for zero yards during Saturday's 35-6 win against Texas A&M. He also had nine rushes for 41 yards with two touchdowns.
impact: Clark came in as starter Sam Leavitt got a bit banged up. Clark struggled a bit through the air as he didn't complete a pass but was able to find the end zone twice with his legs. With McNeese State coming up next week, Clark may be in for some extended action again as the services of Leavitt may not be needed.

headline: Two scores in win
story: Barbie recorded seven rushes for 33 yards and one touchdown and hauled in all two targets for 13 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 36-35 win against Gardner-Webb.
impact: Barbie connected with Carlos Del Rio-Wilson for an eight-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter before running in from five yards out later in the contest. Through four games, Barbie has run for 163 yards and two touchdowns on 35 attempts.

headline: Tosses three TDs in win
story: Del Rio-Wilson was 26-for-38 passing for 386 yards, three touchdowns and one interception during Saturday's 36-35 victory against Gardner-Webb. He also had 14 rushes for 48 yards.
impact: Del Rio-Wilson connected on scores of 48, eight and 34 yards during last Saturday's victory, while also leading the team with 48 rushing yards. Through four games, Del Rio-Wilson has thrown for 756 yards, five touchdowns and one interceptions, while also running for two scores. The Herd have a tough road matchup with James Madison on Saturday.

headline: Explodes for two scores in win
story: Turner-Bradshaw caught seven of eight targets for 131 yards and two touchdowns during Saturday's 36-35 win against Gardner-Webb.
impact: Turner-Bradshaw put the Herd on the board with a 48-yard touchdown in the first quarter before finding the end zone once again in the fourth quarter on a 34-yard touchdown. Through four games, the wideout has 18 receptions, 300 yards and three touchdowns.

headline: Strong day in win
story: Tamarez had three receptions (on four targets) for 96 yards during Saturday's 36-35 victory over Gardner-Webb.
impact: Tamarez appeared in his first game of the season and had a nice day. The wideouts longest catch went for 42 yards in the victory.

headline: DNP Saturday
story: Norton (undisclosed) did not play during Saturday's 36-35 victory over Gardner-Webb.
impact: Norton was held out of Saturday's contest due to an undisclosed injury, marking his first missed game of the season. The 6-foot senior had previously caught 10 passes for 59 scoreless yards through Marshall's first two games. His next chance to return will come against James Madison on Saturday.

headline: Hits paydirt in win
story: Barbie accrued 12 carries for 81 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 30-24 win over Missouri State.
impact: Barbie finally notched his first rushing touchdown three weeks into the season. With just 12 carries in Week 3 and 11 the previous week, he hasn't exactly been a workhorse and that's putting a bit of a ceiling on his production. Still, Barbie has a very favorable matchup in Week 3 against Gardner-Webb.

headline: Scores again for Thundering Herd
story: Lester tallied four carries for 27 yards and hauled in all three targets for 64 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 30-24 win versus Missouri State.
impact: Lester had a rushing touchdown in Week 2, and in Week 3, he found the end zone again this time as a receiver. The tailback isn't garnering a whole lot of touches, as he has just four carries in back-to-back weeks, but his production as a receiver significantly aided his fantasy output against Missouri State.

headline: Solid output in Week 3 win
story: Turner-Bradshaw logged six receptions (on eight targets) for 73 yards during Saturday's 30-24 victory over Missouri State.
impact: Turner-Bradshaw recorded his most receptions and saw his most targets all season in the win against the Bears. The wideout has yet to post an enormous output, but Marshall's passing game has been far from explosive. That certainly puts a lid on how dynamic Turner-Bradshaw can be, but he remains a consistent receiver for the Thundering Herd.

headline: Set to play vs. Missouri State
story: Del Rio-Wilso (shoulder/collarbone) is available and will face Missouri State on Saturday, per Ryan W. Collingwood of the Springfield Daily Citizen
impact: Del Rio-Wilson sat out the second half of Marshall's narrow win over Middle Tennessee in Week 2, but the gunslinger will return to face the Bears in Week 3. The quarterback has totaled 194 passing yards and one touchdown with 73 rushing yards and a score as well.

headline: Could play Saturday
story: Wilkins was three-for-six passing for 23 yards during Saturday's 28-26 victory versus Middle Tennessee State. He also had five rushes for 20 yards.
impact: Wilkins saw action after Carlos Del Rio-Wilson was injured on Saturday. The quarterback split time with Zion Turner and Marshall could opt for the same plan in their next game against Missouri State.

headline: Enters after injury
story: Turner completed five of nine passes for 66 yards during Saturday's 28-26 victory against Middle Tennessee State.
impact: Turner entered the contest following the injury to starter Carlos Del Rio-Wilson and turned in a QB rating of 117.2. Turner has one interception on the season and could be in line to start during Week 3's contest against Missouri State.

headline: Misses second half
story: Del Rio-Wilson (shoulder/collarbone) missed the second half of Saturday's 28-26 win over Middle Tennessee, Tyler Kennett of The Herald Dispatch reports.
impact: Del Rio-Wilson completed seven of eight passes for 92 yards and one touchdown before his departure, along with rushing 10 times for 43 yards. It's unknown how long the starting quarterback will be sidelined, but he'll need to log full practices this week if he hopes to play at Missouri State on Saturday.

headline: Shutout in loss
story: Del Rio-Wilson was 17-for-25 passing for 102 yards during Saturday's 45-0 defeat against Penn State. He also had 13 rushes for 30 yards.
impact: Del Rio-Wilson was held scoreless on Saturday as the Nittany Lions' defense kept the Herd offense in check. Del Rio-Wilson and the Herd have a more favourable matchup on September 12 at home against Middle Tennessee.

headline: Blanked in blowout loss
story: Gladding reeled in 0 of 1 targets for zero yards during Saturday's 54-3 loss to UCLA.
impact: In what was a disaster outing for the Maryland offense as a whole, Gladding was held without a catch as the Terps were blown out as home by UCLA. The 6-foot junior has cooled off following a hot start to the season and will be hoping to get back to his role from the first two weeks. His next opportunity will come when the Terps travel to face Nebraska on Saturday.

headline: Leading receiver in blowout loss
story: Durr logged seven receptions (on 12 targets) for 56 yards during Saturday's 54-3 defeat to UCLA.
impact: On a day in which the Terps totaled just 142 passing yards as a team, Durr still managed to account for the lion's share of receiving work. The 5-foot-11 receiver led the way for Maryland in both receptions and yards on the day, more than doubling the next closest player in the former category. While the Maryland offense can be volatile, Durr seems to have a locked in role as the top option in the passing game. His next opportunity will come against Nebraska on Saturday.

headline: Disaster vs. Bruins
story: Washington completed 18 of 38 passes for 142 yards and four interceptions during Saturday's 54-3 defeat versus UCLA. He also had six rushes for negative two yards.
impact: Washington had the worst game of his young career against UCLA on a day in which the Terps appeared simply outmatched. The 6-foot-5 sophomore threw for a season-low 142 yards without a touchdown and threw for a career-high four interceptions on the day. Better days certainly lie ahead for Washington and the Terps, with the next opportunity coming against Nebraska on Saturday.

headline: Ready to roll as expected
story: Williams (undisclosed) is available for Saturday's game against UCLA, per the Big Ten availability report.
impact: Williams was deemed probable on the availability report leading up to the contest, so his clearance isn't all too surprising. He'll slot in behind Malik Washington as the backup quarterback for the Terps on Saturday.

headline: Upgraded to probable
story: Williams (undisclosed) is probable for Saturday's game against UCLA.
impact: Williams will serve as the backup to starting signal-caller Malik Washington. The probable tag suggests he's likely to suit up, meaning Jack Capaldi should continue in his role as the third-stringer.

headline: Held quiet in defeat
story: Gladding reeled in 3 of 6 targets for 52 yards during Saturday's 35-26 defeat against Virginia Tech.
impact: It was a tough day for Gladding as he caught just 50 percent of his targets and was vastly outpaced in both volume and production by fellow receiver Chris Durr, among others. Gladding had seemingly developed a rapport with quarterback Malik Washington through Maryland's first two contests but largely took a backseat to Durr against Virginia Tech, a situation which will be worth monitoring moving forward. His next chance to bounce back will come against UCLA on Saturday.

headline: Not playing in Week 4
story: Howard (undisclosed) is out for Saturday's game against UCLA.
impact: This will be Howard's second consecutive absence, as he also missed the Week 3 matchup against Virginia Tech. His next chance to play will come in Week 5 against Nebraska. With Howard out, expect AJ Szymanski and JT Taggart to see more snaps at TE behind the starter, Dorian Fleming.

headline: Questionable for Week 4
story: Williams (undisclosed) is questionable for Saturday's game versus UCLA, per the Big Ten availability report.
impact: Williams serves as the backup to starting quarterback Malik Washington, and his availability is in question for Saturday. If he isn't able to suit up, Jack Capaldi is in line to carry the backup duties.

headline: Out vs. UCLA
story: Dalton (undisclosed) is out for Saturday's matchup versus UCLA, per the Big Ten availability report.
impact: Dalton will miss his first game of the season due to an undisclosed issue. The running back has worked his way into the backfield rotation, recording 30 rushing attempts for 113 yards and three touchdowns. His next chance to play will come against Nebraska next Saturday in a Week 5 matchup.

headline: Two scores in defeat
story: Durr reeled in 12 of 15 targets for 109 yards and two touchdowns during Saturday's 35-26 defeat against Virginia Tech.
impact: On a day in which quarterback Malik Washington attempted 43 passes, Durr served as his clear favorite target. The 5-foot-11 junior led the way for the Terps in both receptions and yards on the day while connecting with Washington for a pair of touchdowns in the second and fourth quarters, respectively. Durr has now caught 22 passes for 212 yards and three touchdowns in the last two games for Maryland and appears to be creating separation as the top target in what seems to be an increasingly pass-heavy offense. A home matchup against UCLA on Saturday represents the start of Big Ten play.

headline: Solid day in defeat
story: Webb caught 5 of 7 targets for 98 yards during Saturday's 35-26 defeat versus Virginia Tech.
impact: Despite failing to find the end zone, Webb delivered a productive statline on a day in which quarterback Malik Washington attempted 43 passes. The 6-foot-5 receiver finished second on the team in receiving yards on the day with 98 while catching five passes for the second consecutive game. While he may not be at the top of the pecking order in the receiver room, Maryland's potentially pass-heavy offense could provide a path to relevancy for multiple receivers moving forward, including Webb. A home matchup against UCLA awaits on Saturday.

headline: Scores TD against Tennessee-Martin
story: Chapman reeled in all three targets for 32 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 45-21 victory versus Tennessee-Martin.
impact: Chapman scored his first touchdown of the campaign, hauling in a 26-yard reception. While that catch made up the bulk of his production, the wideout is aiming to become a more reliable target, especially with quarterback Marcus Stokes looking sharp to begin the season.

headline: Reaches century mark in win
story: Thompson totaled six rushes for 110 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 45-21 victory against Tennessee-Martin.
impact: Thomas made his season debut after missing the first three games, seizing his opportunity by surpassing 100 yards on the ground and scoring his first career touchdown. Most of the running back's production came on a 72-yard run in the fourth quarter. Moving forward, the true freshman will likely only see carries in blowout scenarios like this one.

headline: Another game, another touchdown
story: Carter tallied 12 carries for 62 yards and hauled in their only target for 17 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 45-21 win over Tennessee-Martin.
impact: Carter keeps finding the end zone, collecting his seventh total touchdown of the season on a 17-yard reception. The running back logged double-digit carries for the third time this year and could have seen more work, but he ceded carries to fellow running backs because of the blowout.

headline: Tosses four TDs in blowout win
story: Stokes was 26-for-32 passing for 258 yards and four touchdowns during Saturday's 45-21 win versus Tennessee-Martin.
impact: Stokes connected with four different receivers to throw four touchdowns for the first time this season. It was an electric performance for the transfer quarterback, who is playing in his first FBS season and has fared well through his first four starts. He also avoided turnovers after committing one in each of his previous two games to help the team secure the win. Memphis has a bye in Week 4, so his momentum will be put on pause until conference play starts Oct. 3 versus UNC Charlotte.

headline: Sees backup reps
story: Noland completed 2 of 3 passes for 15 yards, one touchdown and one interception during Saturday's 45-21 win against Tennessee-Martin.
impact: Noland lost the quarterback battle to Marcus Stokes during fall camp and hadn't seen action under center this season until Saturday. A comfortable lead heading into the fourth quarter allowed the backup to finish the game for Memphis. His first drive didn't go as planned after he threw an interception, but he redeemed himself on the next offensive possession by connecting with Joshua Joseph for a three-yard touchdown. He will remain the backup to Stokes, but it was still beneficial for him to see live action after appearing in only one game with South Carolina last year.

headline: Finds end zone in victory
story: Tipton (lower body) caught all two targets for 16 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 45-21 victory over Tennessee-Martin.
impact: Tipton's status for Saturday was in question due to a lower-body injury suffered against Boise State last week. The tight end suited up and hauled in his third touchdown of the season, emerging as Marcus Stokes' most reliable pass catcher and a red zone favorite. He will look to keep his momentum rolling next Saturday against conference foe UNC Charlotte.

headline: Finds end zone in easy win
story: Upshaw had two receptions (on three targets) for 31 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 52-3 victory versus Central Michigan.
impact: Upshaw was once again limited to just a handful of catches and yards, but he found the end zone for the second time this season and the first time since the opener. With Malachi Toney and Cooper Barkate leading the way in this receiver room, don't expect big-time production out of Upshaw. Still, this Hurricanes' passing game can sustain several productive pass-catcher each week.

headline: Scores again for Hurricanes
story: Barkate gathered in all four targets for 47 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 52-3 win versus Central Michigan.
impact: Barkate hasn't posted more than 67 receiving yards in a single game for Miami, but the wideout has also scored in three of four contests thus far in 2026. His rapport with Darian Mensah is evident, and he'll look to stay hot at Clemson in Week 5.

headline: Finds end zone in blowout win
story: Mallory totaled five carries for 30 yards and one touchdown and gathered in all two targets for 26 yards during Saturday's 52-3 victory against Central Michigan.
impact: Mallory remained an active part of this Miami ground game with Mark Fletcher (upper body) held out of the Hurricanes' easy win over Central Michigan as a precaution. Upon Fletcher's return, Mallory's role will shrink, but he'll still get a handful of touches each week as he's proven to be a capable back.

headline: Explodes in blowout
story: Wheatley-Humphrey totaled 11 carries for 104 yards and one touchdown and hauled in their only target for seven yards during Saturday's 52-3 win over Central Michigan.
impact: Don't expect Wheatley-Humphrey to get too many more opportunities in a competitive game, but the reserve tailback certainly made the most of his carries against the hapless Chippewas in Week 4.

headline: Shreds Central Michigan
story: Mensah completed 23 of 27 passes for 338 yards and three touchdowns during Saturday's 52-3 win against Central Michigan. He also had four rushes for 21 yards with one touchdown.
impact: Mensah was his typical uber-efficient, highly-productive self against the Chippewas. With 12 incompletions and 14 touchdowns through four games, he still has more touchdown passes than balls that have hit the turf which is absolutely remarkable this late into the season. He also added his first rushing touchdown of the season, but he only has 52 yards on the ground through four contests; don't expect that to become a regular part of his game.

headline: Held out for precautionary measures
story: Fletcher (upper body) was held out for precautionary measures in Saturday's Week 4 matchup against Central Michigan, and he should be available for the Week 5 contest at Clemson on...
impact: Fletcher was expected to play in Week 4, but the coaching staff ultimately held him out as a precaution. The star tailback should be ready to roll for Week 5 against Clemson, where he should resume his regular RB1 duties.

headline: Six carries and two receptions
story: Lyle (not injury related) logged six rushes for 16 yards during Saturday's 52-3 win against Central Michigan.
impact: Lyle will look to enter October with a clean slate after facing driving charges this past month. 2026 marks the running back's third year with Miami, and if 2025 is any indication, the U will look to make use of his versatile skill set in the backfield and as a pass-catching option. Last season, for each game the junior was active, he logged at least three carries. Across six matchups, Lyle also recorded a target all but twice.

headline: Dressed for Saturday's matchup
story: Lyle (not injury related) is dressed and expected to play in Saturday's matchup versus Central Michigan, per Sebastian Font of CanesInsight.
impact: Lyle is expected to make his season debut after sitting out the first three games. Even if he ends up suiting up, Mark Fletcher, CharMar Brown and Javian Mallory could still end up handling the bulk of the workload.

headline: Not playing vs. CMU
story: Fletcher (upper body) won't play Saturday against Central Michigan, according to Adam Lichtenstein of the South Florida Sun Sentinel.
impact: Fletcher was trending toward being available for this Week 4 contest, but the star RB didn't participate in warm-ups Saturday and won't be available after he was spotted in street clothes less than 30 minutes before kickoff. With Fletcher out, expect Javian Mallory and Girard Pringle to get most of the touches in the backfield.

headline: Hauls in TD vs. Wake Forest
story: Lofton caught 5 of 6 targets for 39 yards and one touchdown during Friday's 33-20 win against Wake Forest.
impact: Lofton had been extremely quiet through two games, with just two catches for 23 yards. In Week 3, Miami leaned on the tight end a lot more, quarterback Darian Mensah looked his way six times and he parlayed that into 39 yards and a score. This offense is awash with playmakers; Lofton might not always get the chance to contribute in a big way. Still, it was good to see the tight end get involved in Week 3.

headline: Still has fewer incompletions than TD passes
story: Mensah was 30-for-34 passing for 220 yards and three touchdowns during Friday's 33-20 win over Wake Forest.
impact: Mensah has been simply ridiculous this season. He only threw four incompletions against Wake Forest, and while that was more misfires than the number of touchdowns he tossed for for the first time in 2026, he was still extremely surgical. Miami's playmakers are so dangerous that all he needs to do is sit back and distribute the ball. He has a great chance at another excellent stat-line in Week 4 against Central Michigan. Through three games, Mensah has thrown just eight incompletions -- and 11 touchdowns. He's completing an absurd 90% of his passes.

headline: Figures to be available against CMU
story: Toney (undisclosed) is trending towards playing on Saturday against Central Michigan, per Adam Lichtenstein of the South Florida Sun Sentinel.
impact: Toney was banged up in the Hurricanes' Friday night win over Wake Forest, but the wideout still managed to reel in 12 catches for 114 yards and a score. According to head coach Mario Cristobal, the superstar receiver looks "favorable" to play come Week 4. He's already racked up 28 catches for 444 yards and five touchdowns this fall.

headline: Should be good to go vs. CMU
story: Fletcher (upper body) should be available for Miami's Week 4 clash with Central Michigan, per Adam Lichtenstein of the South Florida Sun Sentinel.
impact: According to head coach Mario Cristobal, "everything looks favorable" with Fletcher and superstar wideout Malachi Toney, both of whom were banged up in the win over Wake Forest on Friday. That's huge news for Miami, as those are the Hurricanes' two best offensive weapons. Fletcher has 230 rushing yards and three touchdowns this fall.

headline: Leads Miami in tackles
story: Brooks made 10 tackles (three solo) in the Dolphins' 24-10 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
impact: Brooks led Miami in tackles while playing all 49 of the team's defensive snaps in the contest. The weakside linebacker also played five special-teams snaps.

headline: Picks Pat in loss
story: Rodriguez logged six tackles (four solo) and one pass defensed for an interception in the Dolphins' 24-10 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
impact: Rodriguez played all 49 defensive snaps for the Dolphins in the contest. The second-round rookie intercepted Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter of the game on a deep throw intended for Rashe Rice, advancing the ball 18 yards to the Miami 47-yard line. The 24-year-old's first career interception did not lead to Dolphins points or a win.

headline: Sees increased snaps in Week 3
story: Bell caught four of seven targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 24-10 loss to the Chiefs.
impact: With Caleb Douglas (ankle) inactive and De'Von Achane suffering a torn ACL in the first half against Kanas City, Bell was one of the biggest beneficiaries from both a playing time and opportunity perspective. His seven targets were tied for second on the team with Greg Dulcich behind Malik Washington's 10. If Douglas needs to miss more time, Bell could again see elevated snaps Sunday against Minnesota.

headline: Sees 12 opportunities in Week 3 loss
story: Washington caught five of 10 targets for 56 yards in Sunday's 24-10 loss to the Chiefs. He rushed two times for five yards.
impact: Washington became the focal point of the offense following De'Von Achane's season-ending torn ACL in the first half. Moving forward, Washington needs to be rostered in all fantasy formats after seeing a combined 12 opportunities against Kansas City. On the season, he's recorded 12 catches for 152 yards on 23 targets. He's also handed three rushing attempts for nine yards.

headline: Looking at May/June season debut
story: Marlins president of baseball operations Peter Bendix said Tuesday that Snelling (elbow) is expected to be throwing off a mound during spring training and should be game-ready by M...
impact: Snelling required an internal brace surgery in May to repair a UCL tear in his left elbow. The recovery time for that type of procedure is shorter than that of a Tommy John rehab, giving Snelling a chance to contribute to the Marlins at some point before the All-Star break. The left-hander yielded three runs in five innings in his major-league debut in 2026, and he's been dominant at Triple-A Jacksonville the last two seasons, authoring a 1.46 ERA and 132:33 K:BB over 98.2 frames.

headline: Game-ready by April/May
story: Marlins president of baseball operations Peter Bendix said Tuesday that Mazur (elbow) should be ready to pitch in games by April or May of next season, Isaac Azout of FishOnFirst.c...
impact: Mazur underwent UCL reconstruction surgery with an internal brace in March. He had been tentatively expected to begin a throwing program in September, though it's unclear whether he's checked that box yet. Mazur might not be an option for the Marlins until around midseason, as he'll likely require time in the minors to knock the rust off.

headline: Visiting doctor about elbow
story: Zuber (elbow) is slated to visit Dr. Keith Meister, Isaac Azout of FishOnFirst.com reports.
impact: Zuber was diagnosed with a right elbow sprain in mid-September, and he'll be examined soon in hopes of gaining further clarity. UCL surgery is a possibility with this type of injury, but it's uncertain at this point whether an operation is likely.

headline: Having sore elbow examined
story: Marlins president of baseball operations Peter Bendix said Tuesday that Marsee will visit Dr. Keith Meister after dealing with left elbow soreness down the stretch of the regular s...
impact: It's unclear how long Marsee's elbow has been bothering him, but more will be known about his status following his visit with Dr. Meister. Marsee did not show signs of being hurt in September, slashing .342/.441/.544 with three home runs and a 10:14 BB:K.

headline: Activated from IL
story: Arquette (undisclosed) was activated from the 7-day injured list Sept. 21.
impact: Arquette missed the last few games of the 2026 season on the shelf. However, he managed to avoid a significant injury and will go into the offseason healthy.

headline: Secures third save
story: Alcantara picked up the save in Sunday's 5-3 win over Atlanta. He allowed no hits or walks while striking out one over an inning.
impact: With Miami opting against having him make one last start over the weekend, Alcantara was deployed as a reliever for the third time this season in Sunday's regular-season finale. The veteran right-hander was able to work through a leadoff error and retire the next three batters in order to secure his third save. Alcantara will end the campaign with a major-league-leading 214 innings, posting a 13-11 record with a 3.87 ERA, 1.23 WHIP and 153:59 K:BB across 36 appearances.

headline: Logs 4.2 innings in no-decision
story: Junk did not factor into the decision Sunday, allowing one run on three hits and a walk over 4.2 innings in a 5-3 win over Atlanta. He struck out five.
impact: Junk's lone blemish was a solo homer surrendered to Mauricio Dubon in the third inning, and the right-hander departed at 64 pitches (44 strikes) after 4.2 frames. The right-handed hurler posted a 4.79 ERA, 1.26 WHIP and 19:5 K:BB across 20.1 innings (five starts) in September. He'll close the 2026 campaign with a 6-9 record, 4.22 ERA, 1.29 WHIP and 89:33 K:BB over 123.2 innings (26 appearances).

headline: Exiting starting nine
story: Lopez is not in the lineup for Sunday's game against Atlanta.
impact: The Marlins are resting several everyday players during Sunday's regular-season finale. Assuming he doesn't appear off the bench Sunday, Lopez will finish his excellent 2026 campaign having slashed .305/.349/.437 with 11 home runs and 34 stolen bases. Javier Sanoja is handling shortstop for the Marlins on Sunday.

headline: Taking seat Sunday
story: Mack is absent from the lineup for Sunday's game versus Atlanta.
impact: Mack will yield to Brian Navarreto at catcher for the regular-season finale. The rookie backstop will finish his first big-league season having slashed .234/.282/.403 with 14 home runs across 105 contests.

headline: Remains out Sunday
story: Stowers (abdomen) remains out of the lineup for Sunday's contest versus Atlanta.
impact: Stowers will finish the regular season having been held out of the lineup for the final four games due to an abdominal injury, though he did appear once as a pinch hitter during that span. It's not an injury that should linger too far into the offseason for Stowers, who finishes with a .239/.331/.459 batting line and 21 home runs in 2026.

headline: Scores in defeat
story: Patterson notched 16 carries for 54 yards and one touchdown and caught their only target for three yards during Saturday's 31-13 loss versus Nebraska.
impact: Patterson was thrust into a larger role due to the injury to Cam Edwards, and he put up a solid performance in relief. The 5-foot-10 senior ran for a season-high 54 yards and found the end zone on a two-yard plunge in the second quarter, bringing the Spartans within seven points at the time. With Edwards being officially ruled out for the rest of the season, Patterson may be in line to see an expanded role moving forward. His next chance will come against Wisconsin on Saturday.

headline: Another tough outing
story: Milivojevic was 18-for-26 passing for 208 yards and one interception during Saturday's 31-13 defeat to Nebraska. He also had six rushes for -24 yards with a lost fumble.
impact: Milivojevic had another tough day as the Michigan State offense struggled to get things going all day against Nebraska. The 6-foot-3 quarterback failed to find the end zone for the second straight week while contributing a pair of turnovers on the day. He will hope for better days moving forward, with his next chance coming against Wisconsin on Saturday.

headline: Out for the season
story: Edwards (knee) is out for the remainder of Michigan State's season , per Connor Earegood of The Detroit News.
impact: Edwards was knocked out of Michigan State's loss to Nebraska and was carted off the field. Later, he was spotted on crutches, so it's not all that surprising that the tailback's injury is severe. Still, this is a huge blow to the Spartans offense as they lose their best player who had posted 339 total yards and four touchdowns thus far in 2026. In his stead, expect Jaziun Patterson and Marvis Parrish to hold down Michigan State's backfield, although they have a tough matchup right out of the gate on the road at Wisconsin's stifling run defense.

headline: Spotted on crutches
story: Edwards (knee) was spotted on crutches during Saturday's matchup versus Nebraska, DeSherion McBroom of WLNS reports.
impact: Edwards was carted off the field with a knee injury that is serious enough to require him to use crutches. If he's forced to miss next week's matchup versus Wisconsin, Jaziun Patterson and Marvis Parrish would be be line for increased playing time.

headline: Done for the day
story: Edwards (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Saturday's matchup versus Nebraska, per Noah Sacco of KETV reports.
impact: Edwards is done for the day after being carted off the field due to a knee injury. In his absence, should see increased playing time Jaziun Patterson and Marvis Parrish.

headline: Carted off Saturday
story: Edwards required a cart leaving the field Saturday against Nebraska due to an apparent knee injury, Ben Shockley of News 10 Lansing reports.
impact: Edwards tallied just four carries for 16 yards and a catch for 23 yards prior to departing the contest. It certainly seems unlikely he'll make a return to Saturday's contest, given the nature of his departure. Assuming that's the case, look for Jaziun Patterson and Marvis Parrish to see more work in the backfield.

headline: Good to go vs. Nebraska
story: Smith (undisclosed) is off the injury report ahead of Saturday's contest versus Nebraska, per the Big Ten availability report.
impact: Smith has recovered from an undisclosed issue and will return Saturday after missing last week's matchup against Notre Dame. The wideout has recorded just one reception for 10 yards this season, so he will aim to become a bigger contributor in the passing attack now that he is healthy.

headline: Out vs. Nebraska
story: Coyne (undisclosed) is out for Saturday's game versus Nebraska, per the Big Ten availability report.
impact: Coyne saw snaps in Michigan State's first three contests but is slated to miss his first game of the season. The fullback will aim to return against Wisconsin in Week 5.

headline: Questionable for Week 4
story: Smith is listed as questionable ahead of Saturday's matchup against the Cornhuskers.
impact: After missing last week's matchup against Notre Dame, Smith's status is in jeopardy ahead of Saturday's Big Ten opener against Nebraska. The wide receiver has recorded just one catch for 10 yards this season.

headline: Huge day in defeat
story: Buchanan hauled in 5 of 7 targets for 130 yards and two touchdowns during Saturday's 20-19 defeat versus Iowa.
impact: Buchanan was a major bright spot for the Wolverines against Iowa, leading the team with a season-high 130 yards to go along wiht a pair of touchdowns. The 6-foot-4 receiver connected with quarterback Bryce Underwood for scoring strikes from 18 and 49 yards out in the first and fourth quarters, respectively, marking his third and ofurth touchdowns of the season. He will hope to continue his positive momentum moving forward, with his next chance coming against Minnesota on Saturday.

headline: Productive in defeat
story: Marsh recorded seven receptions (on 12 targets) for 106 yards during Saturday's 20-19 defeat against Iowa.
impact: Despite the loss, Marsh had another big performance for the Wolverines, crossing the century mark in receiving yards for the second consecutive game while leading the team with seven receptions. The 6-foot-1 sophomore started the season slow, with just five catches for 28 scoreless yards through Michigan's first two games, but has since caught fire, totaling 17 receptions for 211 yards and a touchdown in the team's last two contests. He will hope to continue his positive momentum when the Wolverines travel to face Minnesota on Saturday.

headline: Season-high passing yards in loss
story: Underwood completed 17 of 28 passes for 276 yards, two touchdowns and one interception during Saturday's 20-19 loss against Iowa. He also had 14 rushes for 36 yards.
impact: Despite the loss, it seemed like Underwood took another slight step forward with his arm against a tough Iowa defense, throwing for a season-high 276 yards and two touchdowns to go along with an interception. The 6-foot-4 sophomore connected with receiver JJ Buchanan on a pair of scoring strikes, from 18 and 49 yards out in the first and fourth quarters, respectively. His next opportunity will come against Minnesota on Saturday.

headline: Full-go in workout
story: Vaughn (illness) has been cleared to go through a full team workout with the Brewers on Tuesday, Curt Hogg of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reports.
impact: Vaughn last played in a game Sept. 19, as he dealt with a stomach bug that caused him to lose 10 pounds. He is now considered fully healthy and will be included on the Brewers' NLDS roster, likely seeing some opportunities against left-handers.

headline: Awaiting clearance for mound work
story: Woodruff (shoulder) completed the flat-ground portion of his throwing program Sunday and is awaiting to receive clearance to throw off the mound, Adam McCalvy of MLB.com reports.
impact: The veteran hurler is working his way back from a capsule strain in his right shoulder, an injury that was initially expected to require surgery before Woodruff healed more quickly than anticipated. If Woodruff gains clearance for mound work -- which isn't a given -- the right-hander could have a small chance to pitch at some point in the postseason.

headline: Back at full strength
story: Williams (wrist) was activated from the 7-day injured list Sept. 21.
impact: Williams missed time down the stretch of the regular season at Triple-A due to a wrist issue, but he's managed to make a full recovery. He's expected to see action playing in the Arizona Fall League, per Jack Vita of the Los Angeles Times.

headline: Scores in victory
story: Tracy gathered in all seven targets for 41 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 27-24 victory versus Washington.
impact: Tracy had a solid day for the Golden Gophers, leading the team with seven receptions on the day. The 6-foot senior connected with quarterback Drake Lindsey for a six-yard scoring strike in the second quarter, giving Minnesota a 21-7 lead at the time. His next opportunity will come against Michigan on Saturday.

headline: Inefficient in victory
story: Taylor posted 19 rushes for 36 yards and caught all four targets for 36 yards during Saturday's 27-24 victory against Washington.
impact: Taylor was largely a non-factor on the ground for Minnesota, totaling just 36 yards on an abysmal 1.9 YPC. He managed to gather some volume as a pass-catcher, but was overall unspectacular on the day once again. He will hope for better days moving forward, with a home matchup against Michigan on Saturday serving as his next opportunity.

headline: Three scores in victory
story: Lindsey was 21-for-29 passing for 204 yards, three touchdowns and one interception during Saturday's 27-24 victory over Washington.
impact: Lindsey had his second consecutive three-touchdown outing for Minnesota as the Golden Gophers took down Washington on Saturday. The 6-foot-5 junior threw all three of his scores in the first half, connecting with receivers Quayd Hendryx, Jalen Smith and Javon Tracy to build an early lead for the Gophers. Lindsey will look to continue his positive momentum as the season progresses, with a home battle against Michigan serving as his next opportunity.

headline: Available vs. Washington
story: Bates (undisclosed) is available for Saturday's game at Washington.
impact: Bates has yet to see a snap this season. Even if he's cleared to play after his injury, he's buried on the depth chart, so he's not likely to be an option in the backfield either way.

headline: Officially available vs. Washington
story: Taylor (undisclosed) is available for Saturday's game at Washington, per the Big Ten availability report.
impact: Taylor is set to suit up Saturday and lead the Gophers' backfield after a one-game absence. The running back has recorded 71 rushing yards for three touchdowns on 20 attempts this season. TJ Thomas is expected to serve as the backup once again.

headline: Probable for Saturday
story: Bates (undisclosed) is probable for Saturday's game at Washington.
impact: Bates has yet to see a snap this season as he battles through an undisclosed injury from fall camp. Even when healthy, Bates is expected to serve as a depth option in the Gopher running back room.

headline: Out vs. Washington
story: Moore (undisclosed) is out for Saturday's contest at Washington, per the Big Ten availability report.
impact: Moore is set to miss his second consecutive game due to an undisclosed issue. The wideout has been involved in Minnesota's passing attack this season, catching three passes for 49 yards in the first two games. He will look to make his return during next week's matchup against Michigan.

headline: Listed as probable for Saturday
story: Taylor (undisclosed) is probable for Saturday's game at Washington, per the Big Ten availability report.
impact: Taylor missed last week's game after he was seen warming up with other injured players, but is trending in the right direction to be ready for Minnesota's Big Ten opener, which will help bolster the backfield. In two games this season he has recorded 20 rushing attempts for 71 yards and three touchdowns.

headline: Leading receiver vs. Akron
story: Tracy notched five receptions (on six targets) for 91 yards during Saturday's 41-7 victory versus Akron.
impact: Tracy led the way for Minnesota receivers on the day, pacing the team in receiving yards while tying for the team lead with five receptions against the Zips. Though the 6-foot senior was held scoreless ont he day, his continued involvement in the passing game in encouraging to see, as he has now logged 23 targets across three contests for the Golden Gophers. He will hope to continue the trend as the team travels to Seattle to face Washington to kick off the start of conference play.

headline: Leading runner in victory
story: Thomas logged 13 rushes for 122 yards and one touchdown and hauled in 3 of 5 targets for negative eight yards during Saturday's 41-7 victory versus Akron.
impact: With Darius Taylor sidelined due to injury, Thomas made the most of his extended opportunities. The 5-foot-8 running back showed off his explosive ability, scoring on a 71-yard scamper in the fourth quarter to extend the Minnesota lead while averaging an exceptional 9.4 YPC. When Taylor is able to return, Thomas' opportunities will likely dwindle, though he will be hoping his performance on Saturday could at least earn him a share of touches moving forward.

headline: Scores in blowout win
story: Turner recorded eight rushes for 40 yards and one touchdown and caught 0 of 1 targets for zero yards during Saturday's 41-7 victory against Akron.
impact: On a day in which starter Darius Taylor was out due to injury, Turner took advantage of his expanded opportunities in the running game. The 6-foot senior found the end zone on a four-yard scamper in the fourth quarter, extending the already insurmountable Minnesota lead. While his inclusion in the gameplan was nice to see, the blowout nature of the game likely provided an avenue for extended opportunities, and Taylor's potential return would likely cause Turner's touches to dwindle further.

headline: Homer, three RBI in finale
story: Bell went 1-for-3 with a home run, a walk and three RBI in Sunday's 6-4 win over the Rangers.
impact: Bell opened the scoring with a sacrifice fly in the first inning before adding a two-run shot in the third. It ends a solid campaign for the 34-year-old, who took a one-year deal with the Twins and led the team with 96 RBI, his highest total since 2019. Additionally, he slashed .255/.319/.419 with 21 homers, 78 runs scored and two steals across 631 plate appearances and may enter free agency despite having a mutual option for 2027.

headline: Homer, steal in finale
story: Lewis went 2-for-4 with a solo home run and a stolen base in Sunday's 6-4 win over the Rangers.
impact: Lewis launched a solo shot in the eighth inning, tallying his second game with a homer and a steal this season. It was a nice end to an otherwise forgettable September in which he hit just .209 with two home runs and 11 RBI. Overall, the 27-year-old finished an inconsistent campaign slashing .227/.287/.380 with 15 long balls, 57 RBI, 51 runs scored and 16 stolen bases across 509 plate appearances.

headline: Goes seven strong in win
story: Kremer (5-5) earned the win against the Rangers on Sunday, allowing one run on three hits and no walks with four strikeouts over seven innings.
impact: Kremer was spotted an early lead and ran with it, with a solo homer in the third inning serving as his only blemish. The 30-year-old ended his season on a nice run, finishing September 3-0 while yielding just four earned runs over his final four outings. Overall, he'll conclude the campaign with a 4.68 ERA, 1.14 WHIP and 86:29 K:BB across 90.1 innings with the Orioles and Twins.

headline: Finishes with nine stops in Week 3
story: Metellus recorded nine tackles (four solo), including 0.5 sacks, and a defensed pass Sunday against Tampa Bay in a 23-16 victory.
impact: Metellus logged the second-most tackles on Minnesota behind Eric Wilson (11). One of his stops was an assisted sack of Baker Mayfield on the first play of the fourth quarter. Metellus has played every defensive snap for the Vikings so far this season and has racked up 20 tackles and two pass defenses through three contests.

headline: Seals Week 3 win with pickoff
story: Rodgers logged six tackles (two solo) and an interception in Sunday's 23-16 victory over Tampa Bay.
impact: Minnesota led by seven points late in the fourth quarter when Rodgers picked off rookie Jalon Daniels on a last-second heave that drifted just short of the end zone. It was Rodgers' first interception of the season and the fifth of his six-year career. The veteran cornerback emerged as a key starter for Minnesota last season and has played nearly every defensive snap for the team so far in 2026.

headline: Registers another sack in Week 3 victory
story: Cashman tallied eight tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, and defensed a pass Sunday in a 23-16 win against the Buccaneers.
impact: Cashman tied for third on Minnesota in stops and tied for the team lead with a pair of QB hits. He also brought down Bucs QB Baker Mayfield for a 10-yard loss early in the fourth quarter. Cashman is thriving in the Vikings' blitz-happy system with 2.5 sacks through three games. His career best is 4.5 sacks set over 14 regular-season contests in 2024.

headline: Overwhelms Bucs in Week 3
story: Wilson finished Sunday's 23-16 victory over Tampa Bay with 10 tackles, including 1.5 sacks, and one defensed pass.
impact: Wilson not only led Minnesota with 10 stops, he was also responsible for 1.5 of the team's six total sacks. The veteran linebacker recorded a career-high 6.5 sacks across 17 regular-season games with the Vikings last year, as he's benefitted statistically from being in defensive coordinator Brian Flores' blitz-happy system. Wilson also surpassed 100 tackles for the second time in his career last year and is on pace to do so again in 2026 with 20 stops through three contests.

headline: Placed on injured reserve
story: The Vikings placed Oliver (biceps) on injured reserve Tuesday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
impact: Oliver's move to IR was expected after the tight end was diagnosed with a torn bicep Monday. The tight end will likely miss most, if not all, of the 2026 season as he recovers from surgery. T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew are now the only tight ends on the Vikings' roster, meaning practice squad elevations ahead of Week 5 will likely include at least one more option for the team. The Vikings signed linebacker Kyle Van Noy to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

headline: Promoted to active roster
story: The Vikings signed Van Noy from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
impact: The Vikings burned through Van Noy's practice squad elevations by playing the veteran linebacker in each of the team's three wins to start the 2026 regular season. Van Noy logged 59 defensive snaps over the three contests, totaling seven tackles (five solo), including 1.5 sacks. The 35-year-old will now stay a key rotational edge rusher for the team, this time on the 53-man roster.

headline: Receives promotion from practice squad
story: The Vikings will sign Brosmer off their practice squad Tuesday, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
impact: With the Vikings trading J.J. McCarthy to the Giants on Monday, Brosmer will be awarded a spot on the 53-man roster and slot in as the team's No. 3 quarterback behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz. As an undrafted rookie last season, Brosmer appeared in eight games for the Vikings and completed 47 of 71 pass attempts for 328 yards, zero touchdowns and four interceptions while carrying seven times for 11 yards and also losing a fumble.

headline: Minimal output in win
story: Ragins logged two receptions (on three targets) for 14 yards during Saturday's 31-24 victory against Missouri.
impact: Ragins took a back seat to Anthony Evans and Sanfrisco Magee as quarterback Kamario Taylor spread the ball around . The redshirt sophomore has totaled at least two receptions in each of this year's game and will aim to extend that streak against Alabama.

headline: Scores twice in win
story: Magee had three receptions (on four targets) for 76 yards and two touchdowns during Saturday's 31-24 victory versus Missouri.
impact: Magee turned limited volume into a monster efficiency day, averaging 25.3 yards-per-reception with two trips to the end zone. The redshirt sophomore wide receiver has scored in every game this season and will surely aim to extend his streak during next week's meeting with Alabama,

headline: Break 100 in win
story: Evans compiled eight receptions (on 11 targets) for 114 yards during Saturday's 31-24 victory against Missouri.
impact: Evans led Mississippi State in both receptions and receiving yards, registering his third 100-yard performance in the last four games. The senior wide receiver has totaled at least six receptions in every game this season and will aim to extend that stream during next week's meeting with Alabama.

headline: Impressive performance in win
story: Bothwell posted 25 carries for 122 yards and one touchdown and reeled in 6 of 7 targets for 55 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 31-24 victory versus Missouri.
impact: Bothwell handled a massive workload with 31 touches for 177 total yards with two touchdowns, including an 11-yard receiving score in the first quarter.The junior running back has finished with more than 100 rushing yards in three consecutive games and will aim to extend that streak against Alabama in next week's contest.

headline: Impressive performance in win
story: Taylor was 27-for-38 passing for 360 yards, three touchdowns and one interception during Saturday's 31-24 victory over Missouri. He also had 10 rushes for seven yards.
impact: Taylor established a new season-high in passing yards and delivered when Mississippi State needed him most. After the Bulldogs fell behind, the sophomore quarterback led two fourth-quarter touchdown drives, including the game-winning 24-yard touchdown pass to Sanfrisco Magee. He has back-to-back games with over 250 passing yards and will aim to extend the streak agains Alabama in next week's game.

headline: Not playing Week 4
story: Williams (undisclosed) is listed as out ahead of Saturday's matchup against Missouri.
impact: Williams will miss Saturday's matchup with the Tigers due to an undisclosed injury. The wide receiver will miss his fourth consecutive game to start the season.

headline: Finds end zone
story: Hipp had three catches for 18 yards and a score Saturday versus SMU.
impact: Given that prior to this game the tight end had four catches for 20 yards on the season, this was likely a bit of a fluke, especially since backup QB Henry Belin threw him the touchdown pass.

headline: Breaks off big run
story: Dubar ran seven times for 76 yards against SMU on Saturday.
impact: A lot of this damage was done on a single 49-yard run, but otherwise the Boise State transfer was only slightly better than Ramone Green, who still got more touches in this game.

headline: Throws TD, INT
story: Belin went 7-for-15 for 69 yards, one touchdown, and one interception against SMU on Saturday.
impact: Belin saw his first real action this season as Skyler Locklear was sacked six times due to a mismatch between pass rush and pass protection in this one. Indeed, Belin himself took a sack for a loss of 10 yards, and also didn't play terribly well. Locklear, presuming good health, shouldn't be worried about his job for now.

headline: Reception at SMU
story: Cope (undisclosed) logged a 15-yard reception during Saturday's 34-24 loss at SMU.
impact: For 2026, Cope's latest reception marks his first. The wide receiver finished last season with 20 catches for 269 yards. Reaching both tallies will be difficult, but not impossible, for Cope.

headline: Throws TD against SMU
story: Locklear went 15-for-19 for 102 yards and a touchdown against SMU on Saturday.
impact: Henry Belin did get time under center as well, owing less to Locklear's day throwing the ball and more to the fact he was sacked six times. Right now there isn't a strong reason to think Locklear is losing his grip on the job heading into conference play.

headline: Perfectly fine in Week 4
story: Dubar (lower body) logged seven carries for 76 yards and reeled in 1 of 2 targets for three yards during Saturday's 34-24 loss at SMU.
impact: Even though Dubar tied his season-low in carries on Saturday, he performed admirably. With receiving yards added, the running back updated his season-high in all-purpose yardage. This season, Dubar has 218 total yards, his highest tally since 2023, when he was enrolled at Boise State.

headline: Out vs. SMU
story: Robinson (undisclosed) is out for Saturday's game at SMU, per Ryan W. Collingwood of the Springfield Daily Citizen.
impact: Robinson won't be an option in the passing attack Saturday as he deals with an undisclosed issue. Mekhi Miller and Brendon McQueen should see an increase in targets. The wideout will look to recover in time for the team's next matchup against Western Kentucky next Thursday.

headline: Sits out again
story: Cope (undisclosed) didn't play in Saturday's 30-24 defeat to Marshall.
impact: Cope's status was questionable heading into Saturday, and he ultimately didn't take the field for Missouri State. The wideout has now missed two straight games after appearing in the season opener, where he was targeted once. He will continue to recover and aim to return against SMU next Saturday.

headline: Returns with one field goal
story: Obeid (groin) converted one of two field goals and went three of three on extra points during Saturday's 30-24 defeat to Marshall.
impact: Obeid returned from a groin injury that kept him out in Week 2 and reclaimed his starting kicking job. He went perfect on extra points but missed a 22-yard field goal in the second quarter after it was blocked by a Marshall player.

headline: Has 39 yards receiving
story: Robinson caught three passes for 39 yards and ran twice for 13 yards versus Marshall on Saturday.
impact: The proof that transfer Isaiah Myers is now the top receiver came in this game for Missouri State. Once again Myers was over 140 yards and got more targets and receptions than Robinson, who has fallen into a secondary role after being the top guy in 2025.

headline: Another big game
story: Myers caught seven passes for 141 yards against Marshall on Saturday.
impact: Myers did nothing against Texas A&M in the opener, but it now seems clear that was about the opponent and the situation. In the two games since, the WKU transfer has 12 catches for 296 yards and a touchdown.

headline: Over 100 total yards
story: Green ran 15 times for 76 yards and caught two passes for 28 yards Saturday against Marshall.
impact: While these numbers aren't as impressive as what he did against Lindenwood, Green had no issue getting over 100 yards against a proper FBS opponent, and that's a good sign. He was actually a bigger factor in the pass game than the run game in 2025, so expect more on that front as the year continues.

headline: Best game with Bears
story: Locklear went 19-for-28 for 309 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception against Marshall on Saturday. He also ran eight times for 53 yards.
impact: The former UTEP QB definitely had his best game with Missouri State, and possibly the best game of his college career. While definitely an encouraging outing, next up is a trip to SMU, so temper expectations before Missouri State hits conference play.

headline: Helped off the field vs. Marshall
story: Dubar (lower body) was helped off the field during Missouri State's clash with Marshall in Week 3, per Ryan W. Collingwood of the Springfield Daily Citizen.
impact: Dubar was reportedly unable to put any weight on his foot and/or leg, and appeared to be in a lot of pain. The tailback had recorded eight carries for 36 yards and one touchdown, with one catch for five yards, before hobbling off the field.

headline: Considered questionable for Saturday
story: Obeid (groin) is questionable for Saturday's game versus Marshall, Liam Keating of The Springfield News-Leader reports.
impact: Obeid missed last week's contest due to a groin injury, with punter Stewart McDonald taking over kicking duties for the day. McDonald could be called upon again versus Marshall with head coach Casey Williams still considering Obeid questionable. Obeid did not attempt a field goal or PAT in his one appearance this season.

headline: Questionable to face Marshall
story: Cope (undisclosed) is questionable to face Marshall in Week 3, per Ryan W. Collingwood of the Springfield Daily Citizen.
impact: Cope played in the opener against Texas A&M and failed to reel in his one target before sitting out the Week 2 win over Lindenwood. Now, the receiver is in danger of missing two straight games as he continues to deal with an undisclosed injury. Isaiah Myers was the team's leading receiver last week.

headline: Turning into possession WR?
story: Robinson caught five passes for 40 yards against Lindenwood on Saturday.
impact: On the one hand, Robinson had nine catches through two games. On the other hand, though nine catches have gone for 54 yards. Clearly he has a role in this offense, but he may be a possession receiver who doesn't wow with his numbers.

headline: Tallies two TDs
story: Myers had five catches for 155 yards and a touchdown versus Lindenwood on Saturday. He also ran for a 24-yard score.
impact: A Western Kentucky transfer, Myers didn't have a touch in Missouri State's opener. That was against Texas A&M, though, not an easy game to integrate yourself into the offense. This, clearly, is a much better sign.

headline: Finds end zone in loss
story: Olugbode caught 4 of 8 targets for 54 yards and one touchdown during Saturday's 31-24 defeat to Mississippi State.
impact: Olugbode found the end zone on a nine-yard pass from quarterback Austin Simmons, extending his touchdown streak to four consecutive games to begin the season. The sophomore wide receiver will aim to extend his scoring streak during next week's home meeting with the Gators.

headline: Explodes in loss
story: Lee reeled in 11 of 13 targets for 156 yards and two touchdowns during Saturday's 31-24 defeat versus Mississippi State.
impact: Lee erupted for a season-high in catches and receiving yards while connecting with quarterback Austin Simmons for two touchdowns. The senior wide receiver will look to build on this performance for next week's meeting with the Gators.

headline: Leading rusher in loss
story: Roberts accrued 26 carries for 95 yards and hauled in 2 of 3 targets for 38 yards during Saturday's 31-24 defeat to Mississippi State.
impact: Roberts remained Missouri's clear workhorse with 28 touches and 133 scrimmage yards, but was limited him to 3.7 yards-per-carry. The senior running back has seen at least 22 carries in each of his last three outings and will continue to lead the backfield in the absence of Ahmad Hardy. He will face Florida at home next.

headline: Tosses three scores in loss
story: Simmons was 23-for-39 passing for 295 yards and three touchdowns during Saturday's 31-24 loss versus Mississippi State.
impact: Simmons has finished with more than 250 passing yards in three of his last four outings while having his third multi-touchdown game. The senior quarterback has thrown for 11 touchdowns with no turnover so far this season and will keep to maintain his strong ball security against Florida in next week's meeting.

headline: Still has not practiced
story: Hardy (leg) has not practiced yet, making his return to the field weeks away, Pete Thamel of ESPN.com reports.
impact: Hardy has still not practiced this season after suffering a gunshot wound in May. Head coach Eli Drinkwitz said he needs Hardy to have a multi-week ramp up once he does return to practice, so Hardy's return to the field is still weeks away. It's another disappointing update for Hardy after his massive 1,649 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns last season for the Tigers.

headline: Good to go Saturday
story: Brady (knee) is not on the injury report ahead of Saturday's matchup against Mississippi State.
